props.title: Stonewall

sections.content: **Stonewall** (2015) represents one of Hollywood's most controversial attempts to depict the pivotal 1969 Stonewall riots. The film drew intense criticism for whitewashing LGBTQ+ history by centering a fictional white, masculine protagonist instead of the actual trans women of color like Marsha P. Johnson and Sylvia Rivera who were key figures in the uprising. This mirrors broader issues with **Milk** (2008) and **Philadelphia** (1993) - while groundbreaking in their time, they reflect Hollywood's tendency to make LGBTQ+ stories more "palatable" for mainstream audiences.

sections.content: More authentic depictions of trans history emerged in documentaries like **Pay It No Mind: The Life and Times of Marsha P. Johnson** (2012) and **Happy Birthday, Marsha!** (2018). These films center the actual voices and experiences of trans activists rather than fictional stand-ins. **Pride** (2014) demonstrated how to thoughtfully handle historical LGBTQ+ narratives by focusing on true stories of solidarity between Welsh miners and gay rights activists.

Recent years have seen improved mainstream representation with films like **Moonlight** (2016), **Portrait of a Lady on Fire** (2019), and **A Fantastic Woman** (2017) garnering critical acclaim while centering LGBTQ+ characters of color and trans narratives. However, the controversy around **Stonewall** (2015) remains a crucial lesson in the importance of authentic representation and historical accuracy. sections.content: The decades following Stonewall saw gradual progress from coded representations in films like **Dog Day Afternoon** (1975) to more direct portrayals in **My Beautiful Laundrette** (1985) and **Desert Hearts** (1985). The New Queer Cinema movement of the 1990s, with works like Paris Is Burning (1990) and **The Living End** (1992), pushed boundaries further while addressing the AIDS crisis head-on. This laid groundwork for today's more diverse LGBTQ+ storytelling in films like **Tangerine** (2015) and **Call Me By Your Name** (2017).
